Checked every scout-cli-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to 1.30.0-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a development build of the Docker Scout CLI, which for every version lists the same Go release and module versions as the scout-cli package of that version, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read the Go build information (Go release and module versions) of that program in every published package; both architectures agree for every build. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 is v5.18.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.20.4-r2, v5.19.0 in 1.20.4-r3 to 1.20.4-r4, v5.19.1 in 1.21.0-r0 to 1.23.1-r4, v5.19.2 in 1.23.1-r5 to 1.30.0-r1. So every build before 1.23.1-r5 ships an affected release and 1.23.1-r5 and every later build ship a fixed one; the range follows the module version each build ships.

CVE-2026-71556: go-git worktree operations such as clone, checkout and submodule update may follow symlinks in the repository. It is fixed in go-git 5.19.2 by making the worktree filesystem wrapper a symlink-safe boundary (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6213, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-hc8v-wwc9-vgxm, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/releases/tag/v5.19.2). Read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against the repository index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 version in its Go build information, the same on both architectures in each build, is 5.16.5, 5.17.1, 5.18.0, 5.19.0 or 5.19.1 in every build before 0.73.0-r0, which the advisory lists as affected, and 5.19.2 in every build from 0.73.0-r0 on, which it does not; no build contains github.com/go-git/go-git/v6. The function entries in each binary's Go symbol table (go tool nm) include advisory-listed go-git functions in every build, at least PlainCloneContext, (*Submodule).Repository, (*Worktree).Checkout and (*Worktree).checkoutFile, with runtime.main found in every binary as the control.

Read every published trivy package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against the repository index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 version in its Go build information, the same on both architectures in each build, is 5.16.5, 5.17.1, 5.18.0, 5.19.0 or 5.19.1 in every build before 0.73.0-r0, which the advisory lists as affected, and 5.19.2 in every build from 0.73.0-r0 on, which it does not; no build contains github.com/go-git/go-git/v6. The function entries in each binary's Go symbol table (go tool nm) include advisory-listed go-git functions in every build, at least PlainCloneContext, (*Submodule).Repository, (*Worktree).Checkout and (*Worktree).checkoutFile, with runtime.main found in every binary as the control.

CVE-2026-71556 (GHSA-hc8v-wwc9-vgxm, GO-2026-6213): go-git worktree operations followed symbolic links already present in the worktree, so a write through an otherwise valid path could land outside the worktree, for example in the repository .git directory. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 up to 5.19.1 is affected (https://github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-hc8v-wwc9-vgxm); the fix, https://github.com/go-git/go-git/commit/008a78f2dd86f52544ddff8b8e8ddeecdf3f7aab, first ships in v5.19.2 (https://github.com/go-git/go-git/releases/tag/v5.19.2). Checked every scout-cli-dev package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to 1.30.0-1, each for amd64 and arm64. Each installs one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a development build of the Docker Scout CLI, which for every version lists the same Go release and module versions as the scout-cli package of that version; in every build that program carries the same Go build ID (which includes a hash of the linked program) as the Alpine 3.23 scout-cli-dev build of the same version (1.20.4-1 matches 1.20.4-r1, and so on) and architecture, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 whose Go build information (Go release and module versions) we read. github.com/go-git/go-git/v5 is v5.18.0 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-2, v5.19.0 in 1.20.4-3 to 1.20.4-4, v5.19.1 in 1.21.0-0 to 1.23.1-4, v5.19.2 in 1.23.1-5 to 1.30.0-1. So every build before 1.23.1-5 ships an affected release and 1.23.1-5 and every later build ship a fixed one; the range follows the module version each build ships.
